run.scenario: Synthetic evaluation network; not Boston observations. Frozen at 08:00 EDT, September 14. Missing APC, crew, maintenance, fleet, dispatch and historical outcome data are deliberate.

reviews.assessment: Misattributes late predictions to reporting gaps; does not provide a defensible network diagnosis.
Claims close spacing contradicts delay and speculates about control/driver behavior. Suggests a live holding simulation that is not connected.
Extends the Route 39 construction cause to routes 55 and 57, then inconsistently disclaims a shared cause.
Dismisses Route 66's 25-minute predicted gap as a reporting artifact despite cancellation and spacing evidence. Does not establish the asserted cause.
Invents delay onset and actual vehicle progression from same-stop forecast history, and reverses upstream/downstream evidence.
Chooses a trip that was not selected, invents downstream propagation, and declares other late routes unaffected.
Correctly distinguishes the Route 66 gap from bunching, but falsely calls Route 39's multiple close pairs a single bad pair and overstates cause exclusion.
Invents severe crowding and waits above 15 minutes on Route 39, turns a close pair into a single trip, and calls 25 versus 10 double.
Reached the 180-second deadline without an answer; the saved-work fallback does not explain the asserted gap.
Calls Route 39 the Red Line and investigates the wrong route. Missing history is not evidence of ordinary reliability.
Moves the reported cancellation from Route 66 to Route 39.
Treats absent shared-cause notices and unavailable upstream evidence as proof of distinct causes, dismissing the common-disruption hypothesis without counterevidence.
Dismisses the user-reported crash because no matching alert exists, and attributes other-route delay to construction/elevator maintenance.
Invents worsening and no recovery by 90 minutes, treats future non-reporting as failed service and suggests holding closes the gap ahead.
Correctly says there is no calibrated recovery model, but treats a hypothetical clearance as requiring confirmation instead of analyzing conditional recovery dependencies.
Invents a typical construction-delay range and a 20-minute intervention threshold, then recommends no intervention instead of a supported conditional comparison.
No completed answer to either side of the short-turn comparison; only the saved evidence fallback remained.
Repeated the same service inspection and reached the deadline without a spare allocation comparison. A later code change bounds this exact-read loop; this retained run predates it.
Declares any Route 39 connection high-risk without transfer timings and gives an unsupported blanket no-hold decision. Suggests GTFS vehicle reports establish mechanical status.
States demand is not exceeding capacity without passenger data, and extends Route 39 construction to 55/57. Correctly notes one FULL occupancy report is not network demand saturation.
Declares inadequate PM fleet capacity and failed pull-out risk from morning reports, with no fleet requirement or readiness data.
Correctly lists missing crew data later, but first asserts no endangered reliefs and no crew pressure on on-time routes without assignments or duty evidence.

Correctly withholds a fitness decision, but speculates faults may have cleared because there is no public alert, implies telemetry access after an ID lookup, and invents suspension/replacement commitments in an unsolicited draft.
Correctly separates Park Street access from Harvard Square delay, but asserts independent causes and excludes a shared factor without establishing either.
Equates a 14-minute headway increase with 14 extra minutes waiting for each rider; this is not established by the interval.
Does not establish A/B or compute alternatives, ignores the hypothetical suspension and offers generic advice to contact the authority.

Keeps causes scoped and generates one app draft through the tool, but omits the requested station-sign and social-media drafts. The final answer discusses deployment instead of delivering the three drafts.
Identifies the notice's limited scope, but does not complete the affected-stop/direction/accessibility comparison and announces checks it did not execute.

Equates fresh feeds with correct predictions, treats a filtered empty alert search as absence of all notices, assigns a Red Line access issue to Route 66, and claims missing alerts confirm operational truth. A later composition fix retains query filters.
Correctly reports absent historical study/notebook evidence, but describes a filtered current-alert search as a yesterday check and gives a weak retrospective reconstruction plan.
Correctly identifies the scoped construction notice and maximum delay, but falsely says headways remain consistent at 10 minutes despite close-pair evidence.
Projects morning delay into evening-peak travel advice, asserts distinct independent causes without evidence, and omits the needed PM readiness/forecast work.
